info.title: trax
info.description: The `trax` dotnet tool. `trax generate` scaffolds a Trax .NET hub project and a trains library (trains, junctions, input/output records) from a GraphQL SDL or OpenAPI schema; `trax machine new|generate|check` scaffolds a state machine and generates its IR, TypeScript twin and differential corpus from a compiled assembly. Install it with `dotnet tool install Trax.Cli`.

commands.name: generate
commands.description: Generate a Trax API project from a schema file

options.name: --schema
options.description: Path to the schema file (.graphql, .gql, .json, .yaml, .yml)

options.name: --output
options.description: Output directory for the generated project

options.name: --name
options.description: Project name (used for namespace and csproj)

options.name: --type
options.description: Schema type: graphql or openapi (auto-detected from extension if omitted)

options.name: --force
options.description: Replace the output directory if it exists, once generation has succeeded (refused for the current directory, its parents, or a git repository) [default: False]

commands.name: machine
commands.description: Generate and check state-machine artifacts from a compiled Trax machine.

commands.name: new
commands.description: Scaffold a new Tier-1 machine as a single declarative C# file.

options.name: --output
options.description: Directory to write <Name>Machine.cs (default: current directory).

options.name: --namespace
options.description: Namespace for the generated file (default: Machines).

options.name: --with-effect
options.description: Include an exactly-once effect stub and mark the terminal state committed. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite the file if it already exists. [default: False]

commands.name: generate
commands.description: Export the IR from a compiled machine, or read it from a host's client manifest, and generate its typed view (TypeScript or C#) and/or differential corpus.

options.name: --assembly
options.description: Compiled assembly (.dll) containing the machine. Or pass --manifest.

options.name: --manifest
options.description: The client manifest the host exported with --trax-export-client, to read the IR from in place of --assembly: for a frontend that has the manifest and not the server.

options.name: --machine
options.description: Full type name of the machine, or its id with --manifest (required only if there is more than one).

options.name: --ir-out
options.description: Directory to write <id>.ir.json.

options.name: --twin-out
options.description: Directory to write <id>.contexts.g.ts and <id>.machine.g.ts.

options.name: --corpus-out
options.description: Directory to write differential.json.

options.name: --engine-src
options.description: Generate the twin and corpus from this engine checkout's src/ (and the tools/ beside it) instead of the engine bundled into trax.

options.name: --import-style
options.description: Twin engine imports: 'specifier' (default) or 'relative' (default with --engine-src, which it needs).

options.name: --specifier
options.description: Module specifier when --import-style specifier: an npm package name, optionally with a subpath (default @traxsharp/state-machine).

options.name: --tools-dir
options.description: The generators' directory (default: the tools/ beside --engine-src, else the ones bundled into trax). Needs --engine-src.

options.name: --node
options.description: The node executable: an absolute path, or a name looked up on PATH (default: node). Never resolved from the current directory; a relative path is refused, and on Windows so is a .cmd or .bat shim.

options.name: --lang
options.description: The typed view --twin-out writes: 'typescript' (default; <id>.contexts.g.ts and <id>.machine.g.ts) or 'csharp' (<Machine>.g.cs, for Trax.StateMachine.Client).

options.name: --namespace
options.description: The C# view's namespace with --lang csharp (default Trax.Machines).

commands.name: from-gherkin
commands.description: Derive machines from features and their lexicon: their IRs, the host file, the access report and the glossary.

options.name: --features
options.description: Directory of .feature files, read recursively.

options.name: --glossary
options.description: A glossary's JSON file, for features not yet written with a lexicon. Without it, the features directory's lexicon is read.

options.name: --trains
options.description: A train assembly (.dll) the lexicon reads each train's input and output records from, as the host does, so its Returns: and Takes: lines are optional. Repeat for several.

options.name: --out
options.description: Directory the command owns: one <machine>.ir.json per machine, host.json, access.txt and the glossary.json the lexicon elaborates to. A machine that no longer derives has its file removed.

options.name: --check
options.description: Write nothing; exit 1 if any file in --out differs from what the features derive, access.txt included. [default: False]

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run features in memory on the machines a directory serves, access included, answering as the host does.

options.name: --features
options.description: Directory of .feature files, read recursively.

options.name: --glossary
options.description: A glossary's JSON file, for features not yet written with a lexicon. Without it, the features directory's lexicon is read.

options.name: --trains
options.description: A train assembly (.dll) the lexicon reads each train's input and output records from, as the host does, so its Returns: and Takes: lines are optional. Repeat for several.

options.name: --machines
options.description: The directory from-gherkin wrote, as committed: the features run on these machines.

options.name: --tags
options.description: A tag expression: @smoke, '@smoke and not @slow', '(@a or @b) and not @c'.

options.name: --name
options.description: Run only scenarios whose name matches this regular expression. Repeat for any of several.

options.name: --format
options.description: pretty (default), json or junit. [default: pretty]

options.name: --report
options.description: Write the report to this file instead of standard output.

options.name: --strict
options.description: Also fail on steps about the UI, which are not checked here. An undefined step always fails. [default: False]

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Read every step and run none: shows undefined steps. [default: False]

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description: Stop at the first scenario that does not pass. [default: False]

arguments.name: LOCATIONS
arguments.description: Scenarios to run, as file:line relative to --features (a scenario's or an example row's line).

commands.name: client
commands.description: Generate a frontend's typed client from the host's client manifest, or check the committed one.

options.name: --target
options.description: The framework the client is for. Only react is generated today. [default: react]

options.name: --manifest
options.description: The client manifest the host exported with --trax-export-client. Required unless --operations is given.

options.name: --operations
options.description: The operations schema, as SDL, in place of --manifest: generates a client for documents that reach only operations and the operator's streams, as the operations console's do, and the console-documents.json a host registers them from. Needs --documents.

options.name: --out
options.description: The directory the client is written to, inside the frontend's source (src/trax).

options.name: --check
options.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when the client in --out is not what the manifest generates. [default: False]

options.name: --specifier
options.description: The module the client imports the runtime from (default @traxsharp/state-machine).

options.name: --tools-dir
options.description: The engine's tools/ directory, when this trax has no generators bundled (built from source).

options.name: --documents
options.description: A glob of the .graphql documents the frontend wrote (src/**/*.graphql), relative to the current directory. Repeatable. Writes a typed function per operation and trax.documents.json, which the host names in ClientDocuments(path).

options.name: --lang
options.description: With --operations, the language of the client: typescript (default) or csharp, a client over Trax.Client for a .NET operator frontend.

options.name: --namespace
options.description: With --operations --lang csharp, the namespace of the client (default Trax.Operations).

options.name: --node
options.description: The node executable that generates the twins: an absolute path, or a name on PATH (default: node).

commands.name: lexicon
commands.description: Work with lexicons, the files that say what features' words mean.

commands.name: format
commands.description: Lay a lexicon out in one way: two spaces per block, its columns lined up. What it elaborates to is unchanged.

options.name: --check
options.description: Write nothing; exit 1 if a lexicon is not in its layout. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATHS
arguments.description: Lexicon files, or directories searched for *.lexicon (default: the current directory).
